upoaa.note: GOL Title 15 is New York's own statute (major 2009 and 2021 revisions), though it shares UPOAA's durable-by-default rule (§5-1501A).

uhcda.note: Health care proxy law (PHL Art. 29-C) and FHCDA (Art. 29-CC) are New York-specific.

rufadaa.note: EPTL Art. 13-A follows RUFADAA's section structure. The article is titled 'Administration of Digital Assets', not by the uniform name, so ULC enactment status was not confirmed.

revised-uaga.note: PHL Art. 43 is not titled a uniform act. Whether ULC lists New York as enacting the 2006 revision was not verified.

localNames: agent under statutory short form power of attorney

assigned.event: Principal with capacity signs, initials and dates; signature acknowledged and witnessed by two non-agent witnesses; POA substantially conforms to statutory 'Caution to the Principal' and 'Important Information for the Agent'

starts.event: As to each agent, the date the AGENT's signature is acknowledged (co-agents acting together: when all have signed and acknowledged)

ends.event: Principal revokes; agent dies, becomes incapacitated or resigns; purpose accomplished; divorce/annulment ends spouse-agent authority unless POA provides otherwise
Court revokes under GOL §5-1510 or in an Article 81 guardianship (MHL §81.29(d))

transitions.event: Agent signs and signature is acknowledged
conditions: A lapse of time between principal's and agent's acknowledgments, or principal's intervening incapacity, does not invalidate the POA

transitions.event: Guardian appointed: agent accounts to the guardian during the guardianship

patches.diff: Like UPOAA, New York POAs are durable by default (§5-1501A). New York is unusual in that the POA becomes effective as to each agent only when that agent signs and the agent's signature is acknowledged (§5-1501B(3)(a)). Execution requires notarization plus two witnesses. Third parties are protected until they receive actual notice of revocation or termination, including death (§§5-1504, 5-1511).

ends.event: Principal becomes incapacitated, when POA expressly says incapacity terminates it

patches.diff: A New York POA is nondurable only if it expressly says so, for example through the 'Modifications' section of the statutory short form (§§5-1501A, 5-1513).

localNames: power of attorney effective on a contingency

starts.event: Date or contingency named in the document has occurred AND agent's signature has been acknowledged; if the document requires a named person's written declaration, that declaration suffices even if the contingency has not actually occurred

transitions.event: Contingency occurs (or designated person declares it in writing) and agent's signature acknowledged

patches.diff: The springing mechanism is in GOL §5-1501B(3)(b). Like California §4129, a written declaration by a designated person can conclusively satisfy the condition. No default physician trigger was found.

assigned.event: Competent adult signs and dates health care proxy before two adult witnesses (agent cannot witness)

starts.event: Attending practitioner determines, in writing and to a reasonable degree of medical certainty, that principal lacks capacity; consultation required for certain decisions or conditions; notice to principal and agent

ends.event: Attending practitioner determines principal regained capacity
Revocation (oral, written or any act showing specific intent); divorce or legal separation from spouse-agent unless proxy specifies otherwise
Expiration date or condition stated in the proxy
Death, except that the agent ranks first to make an anatomical gift of the decedent's body

transitions.event: Principal objects to determination or decision
conditions: Principal's objection prevails unless a court determines principal lacks capacity

transitions.event: After death, agent may consent to anatomical gift (first priority), subject to written statements in the proxy

patches.diff: Mostly consistent with the UHCDA pattern. In New York the principal's objection prevails unless a court finds incapacity (PHL §2983). The agent keeps post-death authority for anatomical gifts (PHL §4301(2)(a)(i)) but is NOT on the §4201 priority list for disposition of remains, which requires a separate designation.

assigned.event: Adult patient in a hospital (as defined by the Act) or receiving hospice care lacks decision-making capacity and has no health care agent

starts.event: Attending practitioner's initial determination of incapacity (with concurring determination as required) and identification of the surrogate

ends.event: Attending practitioner determines patient regained decision-making capacity

transitions.event: Surrogate identified from highest reasonably available, willing and competent class
conditions: (a) Article 81 guardian authorized for health care; (b) spouse (not legally separated) or domestic partner; (c) adult child; (d) parent; (e) adult sibling; (f) close friend

patches.diff: The FHCDA (PHL Art. 29-CC) is setting-limited: it covers hospital care and hospice decisions and does not apply when a health care agent exists (§2994-b). The priority list resembles UHCDA's but puts an Article 81 guardian first and includes domestic partners and close friends. People with intellectual or developmental disabilities who have SCPA 17-A guardians are governed by SCPA 1750-b instead.

starts.event: Guardian files designation of clerk (and bond if required); clerk issues commission stating specific powers

ends.event: Court discharges guardian or modifies powers when the person regains capacity, dies, or guardianship no longer warranted
Death of incapacitated person: statement of death within 20 days; final report within 150 days

transitions.event: Commission issues (within 5 days after designation and bond filed)
Incapacitated person dies; wind-up under §81.44; discharge under §81.36

patches.diff: Article 81 guardianship is tailored: the person keeps every power not granted to the guardian (§81.29(a)). Authority starts when the commission issues. On death, New York imposes a 20-day deadline to serve a statement of death and a 150-day deadline to deliver property and file the final report (§81.44).

ends.event: After death: guardian may pay funeral expenses and pre-existing bills until an executor or temporary administrator is appointed; must deliver property to PR within 150 days and file final report

transitions.event: Incapacitated person dies: limited post-death payment authority
conditions: Only bills the guardian had authority to pay before death
Until a temporary administrator or executor is appointed

transitions.event: Court modifies, amends or revokes previously executed POA or advance directive
Court grants guardian access to digital assets; custodian discloses catalogue/non-content

patches.diff: New York uses one Article 81 guardian with property-management powers, not a separate conservator. Post-death wind-up follows the §81.44 20-day and 150-day deadlines.

starts.event: Will admitted to probate and named executor qualifies; letters testamentary issue

transitions.event: Preliminary letters testamentary issued pending probate
conditions: Administrator's powers except paying legacies or distributive shares
Revoked by decree denying probate, unreasonable delay, or other cause

patches.diff: SCPA Art. 14 governs. Preliminary letters (SCPA §1412) let a named executor act before probate. No statutory deadline to probate comparable to UPC §3-108 or Texas's 4-year limit was identified (not exhaustively verified).

assigned.event: Surrogate's Court grants letters by priority: spouse, children, grandchildren, either parent, siblings, other distributees (largest share preferred)

patches.diff: The SCPA §1001 priority list is limited to distributees and does not include creditors or a public administrator in subdivision 1. Domestic partners are not listed there.

assigned.event: Eligible person (spouse; adult distributee relatives; guardian of distributee; county chief fiscal officer; named executor if testate) files affidavit and death certificate with Surrogate's Court

starts.event: No waiting period after death; authority evidenced by short certificate. Personal property gross value $50,000 or less (excluding EPTL 5-3.1(a) set-off)

ends.event: Appointment and qualification of another fiduciary (voluntary administrator's powers cease)

transitions.event: Testate estate: if named executor does not act, others may qualify after 30 days from filing of the will

patches.diff: New York uses court-filed voluntary administration (SCPA Art. 13) rather than a UPC-style affidavit given directly to asset holders. There is no waiting period, and the voluntary administrator receives a court short certificate. The limit is $50,000 of personal property, confirmed in SCPA §1301 as retrieved; real property is not covered.

assigned.event: Named in lifetime trust executed and acknowledged (or witnessed) per EPTL 7-1.17

ends.event: On death of sole surviving trustee the trust estate vests in the court (absent contrary terms); court may appoint successor

patches.diff: New York has not adopted the UTC. Lifetime trusts must be executed and acknowledged, or signed before two witnesses, and amendments and revocations take effect on execution (EPTL 7-1.17). When a sole surviving trustee dies, the trust estate vests in the court rather than the trustee's estate (EPTL 7-2.3).

assigned.event: User directs custodian via online tool

starts.event: Written request, death certificate, and certified letters, small-estate affidavit or court order

transitions.event: PR obtains content of electronic communications
conditions: Deceased user consented or court directs

transitions.event: Agent obtains content if POA expressly grants authority; agent supplies affidavit that copy is accurate and power remains in effect
Court grants guardian access; custodian discloses catalogue/non-content

patches.diff: New York enacted Article 13-A, 'Administration of Digital Assets', with RUFADAA's structure. An agent seeking content supplies an affidavit that the POA copy is accurate and still in effect, where RUFADAA uses a certification. Guardians replace conservators (13-A-3.8).

starts.event: After death, absent a donor gift and without actual notice of contrary indications: health care agent first, then §4201 disposition agent, then family classes

patches.diff: PHL §4301(2)(a) ranks the health care agent first and the PHL Art. 42 remains agent second, then family. New York's anatomical gift article (PHL Art. 43) is not titled a Uniform Anatomical Gift Act.

patches.name: Person with right to control disposition of remains
localNames: person designated in a written instrument under PHL §4201
patches.summary: The person who has the right to control disposition of remains and must carry out the decedent's directions where lawful and practicable.

assigned.event: Decedent signs statutory written instrument before two adult witnesses

ends.event: Agent not reasonably available, unwilling or not competent: next class assumes control

ends.note: No explicit statutory end point or day-count forfeiture found in retrieved text.

states.label: Passed to next class / disposition complete

conditions: (i) designated agent; (ii) spouse; (ii-a) domestic partner; (iii) adult child; (iv) either parent; (v) adult sibling; (vi) SCPA 17/17-A or MHL Art. 81 guardian; (vii) other adult distributee (closest first); (viii) estate fiduciary; (ix) close friend or relative with written statement; (x) county chief fiscal officer / public administrator or other person with written statement

transitions.event: Person subject to protection order or criminally charged in connection with death is disqualified (court may waive)
Divorce, legal separation, or end of domestic partnership revokes spouse/partner designation unless decedent specified otherwise in writing

patches.diff: New role. New York uses a stand-alone witnessed designation (PHL §4201(3)). Unlike California, the health care agent is not on the disposition priority list. An Article 81 guardian ranks above distant distributees and the estate fiduciary.
